narrative: Markets are contending with a hotter-than-expected CPI print that has reinforced persistent service-sector inflation and elevated rate hike fears. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan emphasized the necessity of at least two additional 25 basis point rate increases, prompting markets to rapidly price out rate relief. In response, equities are under pressure as high borrowing costs and regulatory scrutiny trigger a sharp reassessment of AI infrastructure and chip valuations. Meanwhile, Diane Swonk warned of the risk of a significant bear market should the broader economy slip into a recession. In commodities, crude oil markets are digesting geopolitical de-escalation regarding Iran alongside volatile supply dynamics.

Nasdaq.why: Tim Urbanowicz of Innovator noted that AI and chip valuations face a significant correction amid rising interest rates and regulatory scrutiny.

S&P 500.why: Diane Swonk of KPMG warned that broader equity valuations face correction risks driven by bubble dynamics, sticky inflation, and high borrowing costs.

Gold.why: Gold was not covered in the provided notes.

Oil.why: Tim Urbanowicz highlighted that oil prices remain volatile due to supply factors and the pricing in of geopolitical de-escalation around Iran.

priced_in: Elevated probability of a December Fed rate hike, with up to 100% odds of 25 bps and discussions of 50 bps or a follow-up in January
No near-term respite from lower interest rates
Equity valuation adjustments incorporating higher AI-related debt and financing expenses
Significant de-escalation of immediate geopolitical risks priced out of oil
